reason: Both satisfy all hard requirements, but Response B's abort/rollback condition is more concrete and directly ties to reversing course (explicitly preparing to restore from the IMMEDIATE ACTIONS snapshot) with measurable triggers (latency worsening >5 min, replication lag spike, disk still climbing), whereas Response A's abort conditions are more diffuse across phases and its detection-phase 'abort' is really just a false-alarm downgrade rather than a true stop-and-reverse trigger. B's mitigation sequencing (re-checking disk%/latency after each reversible step) is also slightly tighter operationally.
